name: NOAA U.S. bathymetry coverage and gap analysis

producer.name: NOAA Integrated Ocean and Coastal Mapping, NCEI and Office of Coast Survey

units.archived_bathymetry_coverage_class: approximately 100 m cell; 1-2 soundings versus 3+ soundings or source footprint

spatial.horizontal_crs: WGS84 geographic service extent; source tiles approximately 100 m

temporal.update_cadence: NOAA indicates biannual compilation; check item modified timestamp monthly and review changes

provenance.access_service: Official NOAA ArcGIS item and MapServer identify
transformations: Checked NOAA's two-class service schema and four isolated Central Coast probes; receipt dist/data/noaa-central-bathymetry-gap-discovery.json
No elevation, native survey cell, fishing polygon or coverage percentage inferred from the class image

evidence.supports: NOAA documents ~100 m classes from post-1960 archived soundings and survey footprints, with source-specific supersession rules.
Official public item identifies this MapServer and says the bathymetry inputs were processed in August 2026.
Live service exposes separate 3-plus-or-footprint and 1-2 sounding-density raster layers.

limitations: Discovery aid only: it does not satisfy the bathymetry need for a fishing spot because it has no elevation, native resolution, datum, uncertainty or valid survey-cell mask.
A 3-plus class may come from a survey footprint assigned that class rather than three observed soundings at the displayed cell.
The four audited point probes do not establish sector-wide coverage. A transparent result is not proof that an area was never surveyed.
No source-grid redistribution or public display is authorized by this source review.
